Topics · Prayer and closeness to God

Does God hear me when I call Him directly?

Direct prayer needs no one to carry it, if God is near, aware and willing. The Quran answers each doubt, and the best objection.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:186

Translation

Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

Direct prayer rests on four things: the One you call is near, knows you, is willing to listen, and can be reached. Try the question from that side: which of these would fail for the One you have in mind? The verse takes up exactly this question. People ask the Prophet about God. In most other places where people ask him something, the reply begins with the word 'say'. Here it does not: the speech is direct, and it begins, I am near.

A question for you

What reason were you given?

If you sayThat I was not worthy to ask directly
ThenHold that reason. A later part speaks to it by name.
If you sayThat I would not know how
ThenThen the question is whether you need a person, or only someone to show you how. A teacher can show the way without standing in the doorway.
If you sayThat this is how it has always been done
ThenCustom explains why something is done. It does not say whether it is needed. That is a question worth asking of any practice, including one you love.
If you sayNobody said so; I only felt it
ThenThen the feeling is the thing to examine, and the next parts take it seriously rather than dismissing it.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا ٱلْإِنسَـٰنَ وَنَعْلَمُ مَا تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِۦ نَفْسُهُۥ ۖ وَنَحْنُ أَقْرَبُ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ حَبْلِ ٱلْوَرِيدِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have already created man and know what his soul whispers to him, and We are closer[1528] to him than [his] jugular vein.

Translator's notes

[1528] In absolute knowledge of everything about him. "We" has also been interpreted to mean the angels who are mentioned in the following verse.

Quran · Qaf 50:16

Translation

You are near, Yahweh. All your commandments are truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב אַתָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וְֽכָל־מִצְוֺתֶ֥יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 119:151

World English Bible

If the One in question knows what you think before you word it, there is nothing for a messenger to report. That settles two of the four at once: He knows you, and He is near. The verse names the nearest thing it can, your own pulse, and says closer than that. Two remain: willing, and able. The next verse speaks to the first.

A question for you

Which of the four is still open for you?

If you sayUnwilling to listen
ThenThat is what the next verse speaks to. It addresses people who feel they have gone too far.
If you sayUnable to be reached
ThenThe verse claims the opposite. Nearer than your own pulse is not a description of something hard to reach.
If you sayNeither, as far as I can tell
ThenThen nothing stands in the way of direct prayer. Something else may remain: shame, habit, or a wish for company. Those are real, and the next parts take them up.
If you sayI am still not sure
ThenThat is fine. Carry the question into the next part.

Part 3 of 4

﴿قُلْ يَـٰعِبَادِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا۟ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا ۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."

Translator's notes

[1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.

Quran · Az-Zumar 39:53

Translation

Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to Yahweh, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.

Original · Hebrew

יַעֲזֹ֤ב רָשָׁע֙ דַּרְכּ֔וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אָ֖וֶן מַחְשְׁבֹתָ֑יו וְיָשֹׁ֤ב אֶל־יְהוָה֙ וִֽירַחֲמֵ֔הוּ וְאֶל־אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ כִּֽי־יַרְבֶּ֥ה לִסְלֽוֹחַ׃

Isaiah · 55:7

World English Bible

The strongest force behind 'I cannot pray to Him myself' is rarely a theory. It is shame: I have done too much to be heard. The verse speaks to that person directly. It addresses people who have gone too far against themselves, calls them 'My servants', and tells them not to despair of mercy, because wrongs are forgiven, all of them. The offer is made to all of them, and the next verse asks that they turn back to Him.

A question for you

When you imagine speaking to God directly, what is the hardest part?

If you sayFeeling I have done too much
ThenThat is the feeling this verse speaks to. It does not say the feeling is baseless. It says the door is not closed by it.
If you sayNot knowing if anyone is listening
ThenThen go back to the first two parts. The claim there is that the call is heard and answered, and that you can test it.
If you sayNot knowing the right words
ThenThe verses here set no required formula. Another question in this series takes it up directly.
If you sayNothing; I already do
ThenThen you already live what this question is about. The next part is for the strongest objection to it.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ۚ وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذ ظَّلَمُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ جَآءُوكَ فَٱسْتَغْفَرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱسْتَغْفَرَ لَهُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ لَوَجَدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ تَوَّابًا رَّحِيمًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allāh. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muḥammad], and asked forgiveness of Allāh and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allāh Accepting of Repentance and Merciful.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:64

Here is the strongest objection, and it comes from the same book. One verse describes people who had wronged themselves coming to the Messenger, so that he would ask forgiveness for them. Does that stop them asking directly? They ask God for forgiveness themselves, and he asks alongside them. His prayer has real worth, and the verse says so. But two ask; one does not ask instead of the other. Asking a friend to pray with you is ordinary. A gate is something else, and here there is none.

A question for you

What does a friend who prays with you give you?

If you sayCompany on the way
ThenYes. Praying together is a gift, and your own call still reaches God directly.
If you sayStrength when I am weak
ThenThat is how believers help one another. And the verse adds that God is near to each of you.
If you sayI am not sure
ThenThen begin today in your own words. He hears the one who calls.

The same in the other books

Translation

‘Call to me, and I will answer you, and will show you great and difficult things, which you don’t know.’

Original · Hebrew

קְרָ֥א אֵלַ֖י וְאֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ וְאַגִּ֧ידָה לְּךָ֛ גְּדֹל֥וֹת וּבְצֻר֖וֹת לֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽם׃

Jeremiah · 33:3

World English Bible

Translation

Call on me in the day of trouble. I will deliver you, and you will honor me.”

Original · Hebrew

וּ֭קְרָאֵנִי בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה אֲ֝חַלֶּצְךָ֗ וּֽתְכַבְּדֵֽנִי׃

the Psalms · 50:15

World English Bible

Translation

“Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you. For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.

Original · Ancient Greek

Αἰτεῖτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· ζητεῖτε, καὶ εὑρήσετε· κρούετε, καὶ ἀνοιγήσεται ὑμῖν. πᾶς γὰρ ὁ αἰτῶν λαμβάνει καὶ ὁ ζητῶν εὑρίσκει καὶ τῷ κρούοντι ἀνοιγήσεται.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 7:7-8

World English Bible

Translation

But from there you shall seek Yahweh your God, and you will find him when you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul.

Original · Hebrew

וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּ֥ם מִשָּׁ֛ם אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ וּמָצָ֑אתָ כִּ֣י תִדְרְשֶׁ֔נּוּ בְּכָל־לְבָבְךָ֖ וּבְכָל־נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 4:29

World English Bible
